patterns.name: Static advisory Alert with non-assertive role
patterns.description: MUI docs: Alert renders role="alert" by default (= aria-live assertive). Dynamically rendered alerts are announced; alerts present at page load are not. Less urgent messages should override with role="status". A disclaimer that appears when the dialog opens is advisory, not urgent. Use role="note" or role="status" (the CodeTab precedent) and make it reachable via the Dialog's aria-describedby and the checkbox's aria-describedby, so screen readers read it in context instead of interrupting.
patterns.codeExample:
<Alert severity="warning" role="note" id="credential-disclaimer">{CREDENTIAL_DISCLAIMER.short}</Alert>
<FormControlLabel control={<Checkbox checked={ack} onChange={e => setAck(e.target.checked)} inputProps={{ 'aria-describedby': 'credential-disclaimer' }} />} label={CREDENTIAL_DISCLAIMER.ackLabel} />

items: VERIFIED (Ironclad, '6 components of clickwrap enforceability'): affirmative action with a box that is NOT pre-checked; prominent notice; digestible language; a distinct consent that is not buried; and backend records of 'time of acceptance, version of agreement, and other data that ties a specific user to an acceptance event'. Without proof of which version was accepted and when, a clickwrap is 'not likely to be enforceable'.

VERIFIED (clickterm, rsign search summaries; secondary sources): records usually also hold IP/user agent and a hash of the exact text shown. Tamper-evidence matters: a record the business could edit afterwards weakens it.

INFERRED: this is an internal employee acknowledgment, not a consumer contract, so contract enforceability is the wrong bar. What it needs is to answer an InfoSec/audit question later: 'who accepted which wording, for which secret on which test, when?' The clickwrap evidence fields map 1:1 onto that question. IP/user agent add little here because identity comes from the BFF-propagated principal. Do not add them unless InfoSec asks.

VERIFIED (codebase): the current create log has no principal (StudioSecretsService.java:138). The repo persists the one existing human acknowledgment (scheduling) as a DB row (V26:154), not a log line.

TRADE-OFF: a log line costs least and adds no infra. Its retention, immutability and queryability depend on the log pipeline (Splunk forwarding/retention for this service is UNKNOWN; not found in repo). A DB row is queryable and joins to the test, but it is mutable by the app and needs a migration. Neither one is tamper-evident on its own.

VERIFIED (NN/g, Confirmation Dialogs): overuse causes habituation ('if you cry wolf too many times, people will stop paying attention'). Wording must say what the risk is, not 'Are you sure?'. Reserve heavier confirmation for rare, high-consequence actions.

VERIFIED (W3C WCAG 2.1 Technique G155): a separate confirmation checkbox in addition to the submit button is a sufficient technique for SC 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data). The checkbox is unchecked by default and placed near submit. Its test procedure expects that submitting without the box 'is rejected and the user is prompted', which means an explanatory message, not only a silent disabled button.
VERIFIED (w3c/wcag discussion #3845, search summary): a disabled submit as the ONLY signal is weak for 3.3.1. Pair it with visible text that explains what is missing.
VERIFIED (MUI Alert docs): the default role=alert is assertive. Alerts present at load are not announced. Use role=status for less urgent messages.

VERIFIED (codebase): StudioScheduleDialog already uses an inline Checkbox acknowledgment that gates an action (canResume), with no modal. Studio uses Alert severity=warning with role=status/note for advisory text. No modal-confirmation pattern is used for acknowledgments in studio.

INFERRED: secret creation is rare (once per credential per test), so a per-creation checkbox carries little fatigue risk. Plain-variable editing is frequent, so FR-3/FR-4 must stay inline and non-blocking (no checkbox, no modal). Otherwise the warning trains users to ignore the one that matters.

VERIFIED New Relic (Security for synthetic monitoring): 'be sure to create a non-personal login specifically for this purpose' because it 'will reduce the risk of unintended personal data exposure'. Collected data should be 'test data created for the purpose of monitoring'.

VERIFIED Datadog (App that requires login guide): 'use an account dedicated to testing with dummy credentials as a general testing best practice'. Store credentials as global variables with 'Hide and obfuscate'. Restrict access with RBAC. Even though storage is encrypted, the dedicated account remains the recommendation.

VERIFIED Checkly (Storing Secrets): 'Use dedicated test users... minimal privileges... Do not use your admin or root user.' 'Make sure you can easily disable or block these users.' Secrets are never shown after save.
VERIFIED Grafana Cloud SM (Manage secrets): values redacted as ***SECRET_REDACTED***. Only Admin/Editor/Checks-writer can use secrets. The page gives NO personal-vs-dedicated guidance.

SYNTHESIS: 3 of 4 vendors explicitly steer to dedicated/non-personal, least-privilege, disable-able accounts. None of the four documents an 'own risk' acknowledgment checkbox; they rely on docs plus RBAC plus masking. That makes an in-product acknowledgment stricter than industry norm. It is defensible for a bank, but not a copied pattern (confidence: medium. I checked docs pages, not product UIs).

VERIFIED (repo grep for functional id / functional account / service account / FID / citi URLs across docs, PRD, ARCH, frontend/src): no Citi functional-ID request process or URL exists. The hits are unrelated: k8s service accounts, BFF 'service accounts' OU note, runner service identity, and example https://www.citi.com targets.

VERIFIED: the frontend has no existing configurable help-link mechanism. Env vars found: VITE_API_BASE_URL, VITE_API_URL, VITE_ENABLE_*, VITE_LOG_LEVEL, VITE_HOST_PORT, VITE_MF_PORT. STUDIO_CAPABILITIES is a frozen constant (studioCapabilities.ts).

recommendations.subject: Acknowledgment evidence fields (OQ-2)
recommendations.rationale: Record per successful create: principal (server-derived, never client-supplied), csiId, environment, testId, secretName, vaultVersion, disclaimerId + disclaimerVersion, disclaimerSha256 (hash of the exact short text + checkbox label as rendered), and a server timestamp. The client sends only {acknowledgedDisclaimerVersion}. The server rejects unknown/old versions with a stable 400 after the 403 check (NFR-4) and never trusts a client timestamp or identity. This answers who/when/which-wording/which-secret: the evidence set from clickwrap practice, without IP/UA.

recommendations.subject: Storage: dedicated audit logger line now; DB row only on InfoSec request
recommendations.rationale: Matches the @pm/@architect default and the GatewayAuditLogger pattern (logger name e.g. studio.secrets.audit), and adds no infra. Emit after vault.create succeeds, so no ack record exists for a secret that was never created. Raise the retention/immutability question with InfoSec. If they need queryable or retained evidence, copy the studio_schedule_uncertainty_ack row shape (acknowledged_by NOT NULL + non-blank CHECK). Either way, keep the value out by construction.

recommendations.subject: Create Secret dialog: inline warning Alert + unchecked checkbox, no modal
recommendations.rationale: G155 plus clickwrap 'affirmative, not pre-checked' plus the codebase StudioScheduleDialog precedent. Place the Alert (severity=warning, role=note or status, with an id) above Value. Put the checkbox next to the Create button, linked via aria-describedby to the Alert. Wire Dialog aria-describedby to the Alert. Keep the codebase's disabled-Create gating, but add visible helper text such as 'Confirm the credential notice to create', so the disabled state is not the only signal (3.3.1). Reset on every open (FR-2). Wording must name the concrete consequences: anyone who can run the test uses it; it appears in run video; it is your identity. Avoid 'Are you sure?' (NN/g).

recommendations.subject: Checkbox or modal on plain variables / per-run warnings
recommendations.rationale: These actions are frequent. Gating them causes habituation that weakens the one acknowledgment that matters (NN/g). Keep FR-3/FR-4 as inline advisory text (Alert/helper text, role=status or static), with no blocking.

recommendations.subject: Disclaimer copy content (placeholder until Legal/InfoSec)
recommendations.rationale: Align with vendor consensus: use a dedicated, non-personal, least-privilege test/functional account that the CSI can disable or rotate (New Relic, Datadog, Checkly). Say why: personal identity, shared execution, video evidence. Then state the own-risk allowance. At most 3 sentences inline (NFR-2); the rest goes in 'Learn more'.

recommendations.subject: OQ-7 link: optional config value, hidden when unset
recommendations.rationale: No Citi URL found, and none should be invented. Put an optional functionalIdRequestUrl field on the versioned disclaimer constant (FR-9), or a VITE_ build-time var following the existing VITE_* convention. Render 'How to request a functional ID' only when it is set and is an https URL. Owner: @pm with Citi IAM. Note the constant approach needs a code change to set it; the env-var approach needs a deploy config change. Recommend the env var so ops/IAM can supply it without a code release (@architect to confirm).

recommendations.subject: Fix NFR-2 metric
recommendations.rationale: Change 'role=alert or aria-live' to 'disclaimer exposed via aria-describedby on the dialog and checkbox; advisory Alerts use role=status/note per Studio convention; checkbox has an accessible name'. role=alert on a static-at-open dialog Alert would either be assertive noise or not be announced at all.
